Journey & Philosophy

Engineering Story

From reverse engineering Android internals to architecting production cross-platform systems.

My engineering journey began with an insatiable curiosity about how software executes beneath the surface.

During high school in 2022, I started in Android reverse engineering using Java—analyzing compiled applications and working directly with Smali bytecode, the low-level representation used by the Android runtime. This gave me deep insight into application internals, lifecycle management, and system-level behaviors from a practical perspective.

Over time, my focus naturally evolved from analyzing existing binaries to architecting resilient, production-ready codebases. In 2024, while studying Business Information Systems, I made a full commitment to Flutter development—combining low-level system understanding with Clean Architecture, reactive streams, and high-performance cross-platform rendering.

"Clean Architecture is not just a folder structure; it's the guarantee that your business logic remains isolated, testable, and completely independent of external framework changes."
2022 — The Foundations

Android Low-Level & Reverse Engineering

Dissected Android APKs, analyzed Smali bytecode, explored Java internals, and mastered system-level Android mechanics.

2024 — Scalable Mobile Architectures

Transition to Flutter & Clean Architecture

Specialized in Flutter, Dart, BLoC pattern, functional programming with Dartz, and building multi-layer modular applications.

2025 - 2026 — Production Systems

Native IME & Real-Time Mobile Systems

Built and shipped complex systems including RCKeyBoard (Custom Android IME with SQLite engine), real-time chat, chess engine, and background audio services.
